claims.statement: BackendProtocolV2 is the current backend contract: it replaces v1's plain-string and raw collection results with structured LsResult, ReadResult, ReadRawResult, GrepResult, and GlobResult values, while sandbox backends add execute(command) and a non-empty id.

Backend operation failures are represented in result fields: read/list/search/glob results may carry error and partial truncation metadata, read results distinguish text and binary content with optional line pagination, and write/edit/delete results carry storage update metadata rather than requiring exceptions as the only failure path.

FileDataV1 stores text as a line array without MIME metadata, whereas FileDataV2 stores text as a string or binary Uint8Array with mimeType; new writes default to v2 but fileFormat v1 remains available for compatibility.

Readers accept legacy and current file data: migrateToFileDataV2 joins v1 lines, derives missing MIME type from the path, and preserves timestamps; MIME classification drives binary reads and causes binary files to be skipped by literal grep.

resolveBackend accepts either a backend instance or deprecated factory, awaits factories, detects sandbox capability, and adapts the result to BackendProtocolV2; filesystem middleware invokes it at tool/request time.

StateBackend stores files in the current LangGraph state for thread-scoped checkpoint persistence; zero-argument instances read through the fresh Pregel read channel and send updates through __pregel_send, while legacy runtime-injected instances return filesUpdate maps for callers to apply.

StateBackend deletion is represented by null markers for the exact key and all nested keys; missing targets return an error, and the middleware converts a non-null filesUpdate into a LangGraph Command rather than treating an external write as a state mutation.

StoreBackend persists file items in LangGraph BaseStore across threads and resolves storage from an explicit store, injected runtime, or execution context; without an available store it raises a configuration error instead of reporting a successful write.

StoreBackend namespace resolution prioritizes explicit namespaces and namespace factories, then assistant identifiers from config/runtime, and finally ["filesystem"]; namespace components are non-empty and restricted to safe identifier characters, and store searches paginate until all results are retrieved.

StoreBackend writes, edits, and successful deletes persist directly through BaseStore and return filesUpdate null; delete batches null-valued store operations for matching keys and descendants and reports store failures in DeleteResult.error.

FilesystemBackend supports concrete local paths and a virtual root mode: rootDir defaults to process.cwd, virtual mode rejects traversal and keeps resolved paths inside the root, and normal mode permits absolute paths while resolving relative paths under cwd.

FilesystemBackend protects local I/O from symlink escapes using O_NOFOLLOW where available and explicit checks otherwise; virtual deletion validates real parents, writes return filesUpdate null, and directory deletion is recursive without following symlink targets.

CompositeBackend routes by longest matching path prefix, strips the route while retaining a leading slash for child calls, and restores route prefixes for listings, searches, glob results, and routed deletion updates; direct routed writes and edits delegate child results without rewriting their returned child path.

CompositeBackend selects one child for ordinary file operations, fans out grep and glob only to routes under the requested search path, preserves total grep maxCount behavior, batches uploads/downloads by child while restoring input paths and order, and delegates execute only to the default sandbox-capable backend.

CompositeBackend performs parent/root deletions sequentially across the base and mounted descendant backends; it stops on non-not-found failure, reports that deletion may be partial without rollback, and rejects a delete if any target lacks delete capability.

The v1 protocol is deprecated and differs from v2 in its lsInfo, plain-string read, raw FileData readRaw, grepRaw array-or-string, and globInfo methods; adaptBackendProtocol wraps or migrates those returns into v2 Result objects, while adaptSandboxProtocol preserves execute and id.

Filesystem middleware rejects path permissions combined with unrestricted command execution unless execution is disabled or every permission path is scoped to a CompositeBackend route, because shell commands can access paths outside path-based rules.
